children: is expanding its retail delivery business in Canada through a deal with Best Buy
. The partnership brings nearly 300 Best Buy locations to Uber Eats ahead of the holidays, with eligible items arriving in as little as 30 minutes, according to Best Buy Canada.

Uber Eats will be Best Buy Canada's exclusive third-party delivery app for the first year. Shoppers can order laptops, headphones, tablets, gaming accessories and chargers from participating stores and track their deliveries in the app. Uber One members can get a $0 delivery fee on eligible orders that meet a minimum purchase requirement.

The Canadian deal follows a U.S. rollout in September 2025 that brought more than 800 Best Buy stores onto Uber Eats. For Uber, the expansion gives customers another reason to open the app when they need something quickly.
For Best Buy, it puts local inventory in front of shoppers who might otherwise start their search on another app, while adding to the retailer's existing delivery options.

The holidays offer an early test of demand for last-minute electronics delivery. The bigger question for Uber is whether shoppers keep ordering after the gift-buying rush, when purchases may shift toward everyday items such as replacement chargers or headphones.

For Best Buy, the value of the deal depends on how many orders it adds beyond what shoppers would have placed through its own website or stores. The companies did not disclose financial terms or order targets in their announcement.

title: Uber Eats Makes Holiday Delivery Push With Best Buy
